Pilot statements say a go-around (rejected landing) was initiated after the second bounce down the runway. However, the engines did not respond when the thrust level were moved forward.

This is the suspicious part. When landing a small jet the thrust levers are generally at flight idle from 50 feet above the ground until touch down. The engines would be spooled down to somewhere around 60% power.

In this condition, asking for takeoff power will require a few seconds for the engines to spool up to around 100% power. Going down a relatively short runway at perhaps 125 mph, those few seconds would be an eternity.

So, did the engines just not respond at all, or did the pilots panic and not give them enough time to reach takeoff thrust.
